title: Teams meeting policy: which meeting features does each user get?
summary: The documented policy behaviour, licensing requirements and administrative controls are supported by Microsoft documentation. Two minor discrepancies between Microsoft's instructions should be acknowledged: the individual-assignment route and the Copilot values listed in the cmdlet reference.

claims.claim: Meeting policy settings can be edited in Teams admin center at Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Edit.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies or Events policies.
2. Choose the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy uses Identity to target an existing meeting policy and setting parameters to change its settings.
claims.quote:
The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet allows administrators to update existing meeting policies that can be assigned to particular users to control Teams features related to meetings.
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity SalesMeetingPolicy -AllowTranscription $True

claims.claim: Group assignment is available at Meetings > Meeting policies > Group policy assignment > Add; the assignment article calls the button Add group.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
To groups: Go to the Group policy assignment tab, select Add, enter the group name, select the policy name, and then select Apply.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Group <group ID> -PolicyName <policy name> -Rank <rank> assigns a meeting policy to a group.
claims.quote: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Group d8ebfa45-0f28-4d2d-9bcc-b158a49e2d17 -PolicyName "Retail Managers Meeting Policy" -Rank 1

claims.claim: Individual meeting-policy assignment is at Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Manage users > Assign users.
claims.quote: To specific users: Select your policy, select Manage users > Assign users, enter the names of specific users in the search bar, select Add, and then select Apply.
claims.fix: Add to this row's note: 'The recording guide gives Manage users > Assign users; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/assign-policies-users-and-groups instead says to select the policy, select Assign users, and then use the Manage users pane.' Keep the documented route and its existing link.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <user> -PolicyName <policy name> assigns a meeting policy to an individual user.
claims.quote:
In this example, we assign a Teams meeting policy named Student Meeting Policy to a user named Reda.
Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity reda@contoso.com -PolicyName "Student Meeting Policy"

claims.claim: The Meeting recording setting is at Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting recording in Teams admin center.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. Turn the Meeting recording toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowCloudRecording $true enables meeting recording for the policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowCloudRecording $true

claims.claim: The Transcription setting is at Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription in Teams admin center.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
3. Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true enables meeting transcription for the policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Live captions can be configured at Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Live captions in Teams admin center.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
3. From the drop-down for Live captions, select Not enabled, but users can enable(default value) or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled prevents live captions for users with the policy.
claims.quote:
To turn off live captions for users with this policy, run the following script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled

claims.claim: The Copilot setting is at Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Copilot in Teams admin center.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. Go to the Recording & transcription section and find the Copilot setting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Enabled sets the policy to allow Only during the meeting Copilot.
claims.quote:
To allow users to use Copilot Only during the meeting in meetings and events created by organizers with this policy:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Enabled

claims.claim: A named meeting policy controls the meeting features available to organisers and participants, including recording, transcription, captions and Copilot.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can use meeting and events policies to control the features that are available to organizers and participants of meetings and events in your organization.

claims.claim: Meeting policies can be managed in Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Depending on the feature, you can manage meeting policies in the Microsoft Teams admin center or through PowerShell.

claims.claim: Meeting policies can be managed with the Teams PowerShell module.
claims.quote: Policies are managed through the Teams Admin Center or the Teams PowerShell module, and changes may take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.claim: Every user has one effective meeting policy.
claims.quote: A user has one effective policy for each policy type.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: The Global (Org-wide default) policy applies when a user has no custom policy assignment directly or through a group.
claims.quote: Users get the global policy unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.claim: Administrators can edit the Global meeting policy.
claims.quote: You can edit the global policy and any custom policies that you create.

claims.claim: Administrators can create custom meeting policies.
claims.quote: You can edit the settings in the global policy or create and assign one or more custom policies.

claims.claim: A user can hold only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Events have recording settings in a separate events policy.
claims.quote: Meetings and events each have their own recording policies that you can manage.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Event transcription is configured separately in events policies.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Events policies.
3. Turn the Transcription for events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off.

claims.where: What it is: Who a setting applies to
claims.claim: Microsoft documents three policy implementation types.
claims.quote:
Policies are implemented in one of the following ways:
Per-organizer
Per-user
Per-organizer and per-user

claims.where: What it is: Who a setting applies to; Why it matters
claims.claim: Participants inherit the organiser's policy for per-organiser settings.
claims.quote: When you implement a per-organizer policy, all participants inherit the policy of the organizer.

claims.where: What it is: Who a setting applies to
claims.claim: Who can bypass the lobby is Microsoft's example of a per-organiser setting.
claims.quote: For example, Who can bypass the lobby is a per-organizer policy

claims.where: What it is: Who a setting applies to
claims.claim: A per-user setting allows or prevents a feature for each user.
claims.quote: When you implement a per-user policy, the policy allows or prevents a given feature for each user.

claims.where: What it is: Who a setting applies to
claims.claim: Meet now in channel meetings is Microsoft's example of a per-user setting.
claims.quote: For example, Meet now in channel meetings is a per-user policy.

claims.where: What it is: Who a setting applies to
claims.claim: A combined setting restricts participants based on both their own policy and the organiser's policy.
claims.quote: When you implement a combination of a per-organizer and per-user policy, certain features are restricted for participants based on their policy and the organizer's policy.

claims.where: What it is: Who a setting applies to; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Meeting recording is Microsoft's example of a combined per-organiser and per-user setting.
claims.quote: For example, Meeting recording is a per-organizer and per-user policy.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets; controls[1].note; controls[2].note; What to check
claims.claim: A direct user assignment takes precedence over group and Global policies.
claims.quote: If a user is directly assigned a policy (either individually or through a batch assignment), that policy takes precedence.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets; Governance controls
claims.claim: Without a direct assignment, a user inherits the highest-ranked group policy assignment of that type.
claims.quote: the user inherits the policy of the group assignment that has the highest ranking.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets
claims.claim: Rank 1 is the highest group-assignment ranking.
claims.quote: Smaller the number, the higher the ranking with 1 being the highest ranking.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets
claims.claim: Teams admin center supports policy assignment to batches of users.
claims.quote: Assign a policy to a batch of users | Assign policies to large sets of users. For example, assign a policy to hundreds or thousands of users in your organization at a time. | The Microsoft Teams admin center or PowerShell cmdlets in the Teams PowerShell module

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets
claims.claim: New-CsBatchPolicyAssignmentOperation submits a batch policy assignment.
claims.quote: You use the New-CsBatchPolicyAssignmentOperation cmdlet to submit a batch of users and the policy that you want to assign.

claims.claim: Both the meeting organiser and the recording initiator need recording permission.
claims.quote: Both the organizer and recording initiator need to have recording permissions to record the meeting or event.

claims.claim: Transcription is both per-organiser and per-user, requiring permission for the organiser and the person starting the recording or transcript.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: The meeting-policy overview and policy-assignment pages state no licence or meter for meeting policies themselves.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams meeting policy licensing price meter policy assignment license'. Read meeting-policies-overview, policy-assignment-overview and assign-policies-users-and-groups on learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams; none states a licence or meter for the policy mechanism.

claims.claim: Copilot in Teams meetings lists an add-on Microsoft Copilot licence for intended users as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: An add-on Microsoft Copilot license for intended users.

claims.claim: Live translated transcription requires the meeting organiser to have Teams Premium.
claims.quote: The meeting or event organizer must have a Teams Premium license for attendees to use live translated transcription.

claims.claim: Live translated captions require the meeting organiser to have Teams Premium.
claims.quote: The meeting or event organizer must have a Teams Premium license for attendees to use live translated captions.

claims.claim: Teams Premium organisers can use meeting options to control who can record and transcribe.
claims.quote: Organizers with a Teams Premium license can use their meeting options to control who can record and transcribe.

claims.claim: Meeting recordings are stored in the organiser's OneDrive or in SharePoint.
claims.quote: It gets uploaded to the meeting organizer's OneDrive (private meetings) or SharePoint (channel meetings).

claims.claim: Transcripts are stored together with recordings in OneDrive or SharePoint.
claims.quote: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risks and limits
claims.claim: AllowCloudRecording does not configure or validate recording storage.
claims.quote: -AllowCloudRecording controls whether users can record meetings; it doesn't configure or validate recording storage.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A direct assignment silently beats a group assignment
claims.claim: A direct assignment must be removed before the user can inherit a group policy of the same type.
claims.quote: you have to remove that policy from the user before they can inherit a policy of the same type from a group.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A direct assignment silently beats a group assignment
claims.claim: Microsoft documents removing direct policy assignments through unassigning policies in bulk.
claims.quote: When you unassign policies in bulk, you're removing policy assignments that were assigned to individual users through direct assignment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps; controls[1].note; What to check
claims.claim: Group policy assignments propagate only to direct members, not members of nested groups.
claims.quote: Group policy assignments are only propagated to users who are direct members of the group. The assignments aren't propagated to members of nested groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps; What to check
claims.claim: Groups with HiddenGroupMembership enabled cannot use group policy assignment.
claims.quote: Groups with the HiddenGroupMembership setting enabled can't use group policy assignment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps
claims.claim: Class Teams have HiddenGroupMembership enabled by default.
claims.quote: Class Teams have this setting enabled by default.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps
claims.claim: Propagation of a group policy assignment to users is a background operation.
claims.quote: the propagation of the policy assignment to members of the group is performed as a background operation and might take some time, depending on the size of the group.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps; Open questions
claims.claim: The group-assignment article gives no group-size-specific propagation time.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams group policy propagation time 50,000'. Read all of learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/assign-policies-users-and-groups: it says propagation might take some time depending on group size, without a size-specific duration.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's general Teams policy guidance says changes may take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: Policies are managed through the Teams Admin Center or the Teams PowerShell module, and changes may take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policies cannot be tidied freely
claims.claim: A policy cannot be deleted while users are assigned to it.
claims.quote: You can't delete a policy if users are assigned to it. You must first assign a different policy to all affected users, and then you can delete the original policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policies cannot be tidied freely
claims.claim: A policy's name cannot be changed after creation.
claims.quote: After you create a policy, its name can't be changed.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An organiser turning Copilot off; What to check
claims.claim: An organiser turning Copilot off in meeting or event options also disables recording.
claims.quote: When organizers turn off Copilot for their meeting or event, recording and transcription are also turned off.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An organiser turning Copilot off; What to check
claims.claim: An organiser turning Copilot off in meeting or event options also disables transcription.
claims.quote: When organizers turn off Copilot for their meeting or event, recording and transcription are also turned off.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An organiser turning Copilot off; What to check
claims.claim: The policy's Copilot Off value sets a default that organisers can override.
claims.quote: Off | Disabled | When organizers with this policy create meetings and events, Copilot's default value in their meeting options is Off. Organizers can change this value to Only during the meeting or During and after the meeting.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Allowing recording does not provide storage
claims.claim: A recording that cannot be uploaded to OneDrive or SharePoint is held in temporary storage.
claims.quote: If a recording can't be uploaded to OneDrive or SharePoint, it's temporarily stored in async media storage

claims.where: Risks and limits: Allowing recording does not provide storage
claims.claim: A recording held in temporary storage must be downloaded within 21 days.
claims.quote: If a recording can't be uploaded to OneDrive or SharePoint, it's temporarily stored in async media storage and must be downloaded within 21 days.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Allowing recording does not provide storage
claims.claim: The temporary recording is deleted if it is not downloaded within that period.
claims.quote: must be downloaded within 21 days. Otherwise, the recording is deleted.

claims.claim: External participants cannot record meetings except through third-party compliance recording.
claims.quote: External participants can't record meetings except when it's a Teams third-party compliance recording.

claims.where: controls[6].governs; Risks and limits: Meeting policy is not events policy
claims.claim: The meeting policy's Copilot setting also governs organisers' default Copilot option for events.
claims.quote: On | Enabled | When organizers with this policy create meetings and events, Copilot's default value in their meeting options is Only during the meeting.

claims.claim: Teams Administrator can manage meeting policies.
claims.quote:
Teams Administrator | Manage the Teams service, and manage and create Microsoft 365 Groups. | Everything in the Microsoft Teams admin center and associated PowerShell controls, including:
- Manage meetings, including meeting policies, configurations, and conference bridges.

claims.claim: Teams Communications Administrator can manage meeting policies.
claims.quote: Teams Communications Administrator | Manage calling and meetings features within the Teams service. | Manage meetings, including meeting policies, configurations, and conference bridges.

claims.claim: Teams Reader provides read-only access to meeting-policy settings.
claims.quote: Teams Reader | Read everything in the Teams admin center, but not update anything | Manage entirety of Teams admin center with READ only view.

claims.claim: The Teams administrator roles discussed here are assigned in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: You can assign users or groups to these roles in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: A group assignment without an explicit ranking gets the lowest ranking.
claims.quote: If you don't specify a ranking, the policy assignment is given the lowest ranking.

claims.claim: Changing a group assignment's ranking in Teams admin center requires removing and re-adding the assignment.
claims.quote: To change the ranking of a group assignment, you need to remove the group policy assignment first. Then, follow the steps above to assign the policy to a group.

claims.claim: PowerShell Grant cmdlets can change the ranking of an existing group assignment.
claims.quote:
After you assign a policy to a group, you can use the appropriate Grant cmdlet to change that group's policy assignment as follows:
- Change the ranking

claims.claim: The Copilot documentation tabulates interactions between transcription policy and Copilot meeting options.
claims.quote: This setting's value affects how, or if, Copilot works for your users. The following table shows how the transcription policy works with the organizer's Copilot in Teams meeting options:

claims.claim: Teams admin center's Activity log shows group policy operations.
claims.quote: The activity log shows network record upload information, group policy operations from Teams admin center and PowerShell

claims.claim: The Activity log shows Teams admin center batch policy assignments involving more than 20 users.
claims.quote: The Activity log shows policy assignments to batches of more than 20 users through the Microsoft Teams admin center from the last 30 days.

claims.claim: The Activity log covers the last 30 days of the documented group and batch policy operations.
claims.quote: The activity log shows network record upload information, group policy operations from Teams admin center and PowerShell, and batch policy operations (for more than 20 users) from the Teams admin center, for the last 30 days.

claims.claim: The recording page documents channel recording download control only through a PowerShell parameter, not an admin-center toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams ChannelRecordingDownload admin center toggle channel recording download'. Read learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meeting-recording, including its download section and PowerShell examples; these document -ChannelRecordingDownload, not a UI toggle.

claims.claim: The cited pages do not name audit events for meeting-policy changes and where those events appear.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams meeting policy audit events changes Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy audit log' and 'Teams meeting policy audit Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy'. Read cited guides; searched Learn's audit-log-activities for meeting policy and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; no matching change event found.

claims.claim: Transcription is on by default for new meeting policies.
claims.quote: Toggle Transcription On or Off. This setting is On by default for new policies.

claims.claim: The live captions policy setting is per-user.
claims.quote: This setting is a per-user policy and applies during a meeting.

claims.claim: DisabledUserOverride permits users to turn live captions on.
claims.quote: Not enabled, but users can enable | DisabledUserOverride | This value is the default setting. Live captions are off by default, but users with this assigned policy can turn on live captions during meetings or events.

claims.claim: The other documented Copilot parameter values are EnabledWithTranscript, EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn and Disabled.
claims.quote:
On with saved transcript required | EnabledWithTranscript
On with transcript saved by default | EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn
Off | Disabled
claims.fix: Append to controls[6].note: 'The feature guide lists these four values; the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference currently lists only Enabled and EnabledWithTranscript.' The reference is https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy#-copilot. Retain the values supported by the feature guide.
